title: Bidirectional Dijkstra: Istanbul-to-You Fast Routes!
description: Watch how Bidirectional Dijkstra shrinks the search space by expanding simultaneously from start and goal. On a real street-graph style layout, the two frontiers meet to reconstruct the shortest path efficiently.
ig_caption:
🧭✨ Ever wonder how a shortest-path engine finds routes *fast* on real streets? In **Kadıköy, Istanbul**, this visualization runs **Bidirectional Dijkstra** 🔁: one Dijkstra grows outward from the start, another grows from the destination, and the moment the frontiers overlap, we stitch the route back together. 

🧠 Technically, Bidirectional Dijkstra maintains two distance labelings and priority queues, each relaxing edges on a **weighted graph** until the combined best-known path is guaranteed optimal—often reducing explored nodes compared to a single-source run. 

🗺️ Real-world map context: treat intersections as vertices and roads as edges (with travel-time or distance weights). Even with complex street connectivity, the meet-in-the-middle strategy leverages the graph structure to focus computation where it matters. 

👉 Want the next video for your city? Comment your neighborhood + an origin/destination and hit Follow for more map-based algorithm drops! 💬🚀
fb_caption:
🚦📍 Shortest paths don’t have to explore the whole map! In **Istanbul (Kadıköy)**, this demo uses **Bidirectional Dijkstra** to search from *both ends* at once, meeting in the middle to efficiently find the optimal route on a weighted street graph. 

Graph idea: intersections = vertices, roads = weighted edges; the algorithm maintains two frontiers and guarantees optimality when the best possible combined path is reached.
